conventions: signal-bar close then next-bar open; every constant a parameter; long side only in pseudocode with `sides`; non-alternating EL swings; rsiVal/atrVal/emaFast/emaSlow are series variables (EL zero-fill in warm-up); helpers highest/lowest = EL Extremes, atr = WFSafe_AvgTrueRange

candidates.name: SwingBoxChannel
candidates.quote: Non-alternating swing low (X = 5-7 bars) that is also the low of last 20-40 bars. Next swing is a swing high (X bars). Channel is identified by neither of those swings being taken out
candidates.description: Horizontal channel (box) from an anchor pair of confirmed X-bar pivots: anchor A is a swing low that is also the lowest low of the Y bars ending at it, and B is the NEXT X-bar pivot after A and is a swing high (ordering LH); or the mirror, A a swing high that is the Y-bar highest high and B the next pivot, a swing low (ordering HL). The box is [chanLow, chanHigh] = the two anchor prices. It is live while no bar since A has traded below chanLow or above chanHigh. Exposes chanLow, chanHigh, ordering, barsAgo(A), barsAgo(B), active.

complexity.reason: Pivot detection plus a latched pivot pair that must persist across bars while inner pivots form inside it.

library_check.evidence: The library's channel rules (ChannelStartRetestEntry, ChannelLineBreakoutFailure, ChannelWidthConvergence, ...; Brooks) project SLOPED trend/channel lines through pivot pairs. Nothing builds a horizontal box from an anchor pivot that is also a window extreme plus the next opposite pivot. RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple is a fixed-window height test, not a pivot box.

notes: Swing ranges from the note: X 5-7 (default 5), Y 20-40 (default 30). The ~50-bar hold is explicitly not required ('don't require 50 bar waiting time').
Concretized 'also the low of last 20-40 bars' as: the anchor's low is the lowest low of the Y bars ENDING AT the anchor bar.
Concretized 'taken out' as a bar trading beyond the level (low below chanLow / high above chanHigh); a bar equal to the level is a hit, not a break.
Either ordering per Brian 2026-11-05 (TRIAGE Decision 7).

LATCHED: once live, a newer qualifying pair does not replace it until it breaks. This is needed by ON-2 and ON-3, whose inner pivots would otherwise re-anchor the box; the replacement policy is an open question.

EL twin: SwingHigh/SwingLow are VERIFIED, but the pair scan needs pivots of either type in time order, so it inlines the pivot scan (the SwingHigh.json construction) rather than calling SwingHigh at variable occurrences.

candidates.name: ChannelFailedSwingFromHitSide
candidates.quote: start at channel top (flip) and look for 2-bar swings that are first low ... and then a high which is lower than the channel high. Once the swing high forms enter short.
candidates.description: Inside a live ON-1-a box, the side hit most recently is the BOTTOM (long side). After that hit a small (2-bar) swing high forms toward the middle, then the first small swing low after it holds above the box bottom; on the bar that confirms that higher small swing low, buy. The short is the mirror: top hit most recently, small swing low, then a small swing high that fails short of the top.
candidates.book_order_type: enter on the bar the swing confirms (market)

complexity.reason: Two pivot strengths, a latched box, and ordering of hit / swing-high / swing-low events in time.

library_check.evidence: No rule reads a failed small swing after a box-side hit. Nearest: ChannelStartRetestEntry (Brooks, a sloped channel's start level retested) and HigherSwingLow (Brooks, two consecutive pivots, no box).

notes: The note describes the short case (top hit most recently); pseudocode is the long mirror per convention.

'Hit' concretized as a bar reaching the box side within touchTolAtr ATRs; default 0 means an exact touch, which on tick-grid data is a bar's extreme equal to the anchor price (the box cannot be exceeded while live).
'2-bar swing' = non-alternating pivot of strength 2 (innerStrength).
Fires once per hit: only the first small swing high after the hit and the first small swing low after it are considered.

candidates.name: ChannelInnerSwingBreakFade
candidates.quote: Wait for an X bar (same variable as channel i.e 5-7) swing to form. If it is a high, enter short the first time a bar touches the line.
candidates.description: Once an ON-1-a box is live, the first X-bar pivot to form inside it (pivot bar newer than anchor B) is examined. Long side: the box has ordering HL (its more recent anchor is the swing LOW) and that first inner pivot is a swing low above the box bottom; buy the first time a bar's low goes below it. Short side (the note): ordering LH, first inner pivot a swing high below the top, short the first time a bar's high goes above it.
candidates.book_order_type: stop (the bar touching the line); mechanized as signal-bar close, next open

complexity.reason: Depends on the latched pivot box and on the order of pivots after its second anchor.

library_check.evidence: FailedSwingBreakoutReversal fires when the low trades below the most recent confirmed swing low AND the bar closes back above it. ON-2 fades the break itself (no close-back requirement), only for the first inner pivot of a live box, and only the side opposite the box's more recent anchor. SwingPointUndercut (Brooks, low at/below the most recent swing low) is the bare form without the box.

notes: Reading confirmed by Brian 2026-11-05: 'short the first time a bar's high goes above that swing high'.
If the first inner pivot is of the other type, there is no setup on that side (the box's ordering picks the side).
Stop-style entry mechanized as: the bar whose low breaks the pivot closes, enter at the next open.

candidates.name: InnerBoxFalseBreakReclaim
candidates.quote: Price closes below ... the inner box but above the outer box. Enter long the first time price closes above the low of the inner box. Inner box must be at least 3x ATR-50 high.
candidates.description: Inside a live ON-1-a box, an inner box is formed by the first X-bar pivot after anchor B and the first opposite-type pivot after that (latched). Its height must be at least K x ATR(50). Long: a close below the inner box low (still inside the outer box), then the first close back above the inner box low. Short mirrors at the inner box high.

complexity.reason: Nested latched pivot boxes plus a close-below / close-back sequence.

library_check.evidence: FailedBreakoutReversal: some bar in the last failBars closed below the lowest low of a fixed window and this bar closes back above it. ON-3's level is a latched inner pivot box inside a pivot channel, with a minimum ATR height, and the break must stay inside the outer box. The close-back trigger is the same shape.

notes: Concretized the 'pair' as the first pivot after the outer box's second anchor and the first opposite-type pivot after it, latched, so pivots made during the false break cannot move the inner box.
'But above the outer box' is implied while the outer box is live (a close below chanLow would need a low below it, which kills the box).
maxWaitBars bounds the scan for the earlier close below; the note gives no bound.

candidates.name: DoubleSwingLevelBreakRetestFail
candidates.quote: Support zone defined by two 7-bar swing lows at similar price ... There is a close below the support line. The very first bar that reenters the area above the support line is the setup bar ... If there is a red candle that closes below the support, that is the signal bar.
candidates.description: Long side (mirror of the note's short): resistance from the two most recent 7-bar swing highs within an ATR tolerance of each other, level R = the higher of the two, not yet closed above. A close above R (the break bar). The first later bar whose low comes back below R is the setup bar. The first green bar closing above R, at or after the setup bar and no later than the 5th bar after the break, is the signal; long. A close below R by any bar after the setup bar (before the signal) invalidates.
candidates.book_order_type: enter on the signal bar's close; mechanized as next open

complexity.reason: Two pivots read as of a past bar, then a four-stage break / re-entry / invalidation / signal sequence.

library_check.evidence: BreakoutLevelRetest: a close within maxWaitBars broke above the most recent swing high and this bar's low pulls back to within a tolerance and holds. ON-4 needs a two-pivot level, requires the retest to trade back THROUGH the level, enters on a green close back beyond it, and is invalidated by a close back inside after the setup bar. DoubleExtremeBreakout (Brooks) has the two-pivot level but enters with the break, in ticks, with no retest.

notes: The note gives the short (support) case; pseudocode is the long mirror.

'Similar price' concretized as an ATR tolerance (levelTolAtr), per MINING. The support line is concretized as the LOWER of the two swing lows (resistance: the higher high); the mean of the two is the alternative.
'Can be high or close that reenters' collapses to the low (short case: high) crossing back, since a close back across implies it.
The setup bar may itself be the signal bar, as the note says.
The pivots are read as of the break bar so that pivots confirmed after the break cannot move the level; EL twin needs an inlined scan (a lagged SwingHigh read is unregistered).

candidates.name: LargeBarDirection
candidates.quote: Situational analysis around big bars (i.e. bar w/ ATR15 >=2) Does the next bar tend to follow through or to reverse?
candidates.description: The bar's range is at least K x ATR(15) and it closed up: long (follow-through). Short on a large down bar. The reverse placement is the 'reverse' half of the study question.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && high[0] - low[0] >= rangeMultiple * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: One ATR accumulator and a single-bar comparison.

library_check.evidence: ClimaxBar(climaxMultiple = 2, atrLength = 15, bodyFraction = 0) is el_gt(close, open) && body >= 0 && range >= 2 x WFSafe ATR(15): the same bars. The direction-agnostic form is BarRangeAtrMultiple(rangeMultiple = 2, atrLookback = 15) (Brooks), useful as a pane-2 condition.

notes: The note is a study question; TRIAGE concretizes it as a bar-range rule plus its reverse.
ClimaxBar's ATR includes the big bar's own true range, as the note's 'ATR15' reading implies nothing else.

candidates.name: RsiBandBreakThenOppositeBar
candidates.quote: Rsi has been within extremes (40-60,35-65,30-70) for last 50 bars. At close of bar the rsi falls below the lower threshold. Enter long on first subsequent bar that closes green. If rsi falls back into range without a green candle the setup is invalidated.
candidates.description: RSI stayed inside a symmetric band around 50 for N bars, then a bar's RSI fell below the band. Long on the first later bar that closes green, provided RSI has stayed below the band on every bar in between. Short mirrors: RSI rises above the band, short on the first red bar.
candidates.book_order_type: next bar after the green close

complexity.reason: RSI series-variable history over a window plus a bounded backward scan.

library_check.origin: AI Book strategies (facd294; external book, not Davey or Brooks)
library_check.evidence: RsiBelowThreshold is the bare RSI-below-T test. ON-7 needs RSI history: the band held for N bars, a break, no re-entry, and a first green bar. No catalog rule reads RSI's own history beyond lag 1 (RsiRising).

notes: Band widths 40-60 / 35-65 / 30-70 map to bandHalfWidth 10 / 15 / 20; symmetric so the short mirror is exact.
RSI length is not given; 14 assumed.
maxWaitBars bounds the wait for the green bar (the note invalidates only on RSI re-entry, so an unbounded wait is possible); needed for Max Bars Back.
RSI history is read off a series variable (EL zero-fill during warm-up applies).
The note asks for the reverse explicitly: the flip toggle.

candidates.name: UndercutOfLowerSwingBelowLevelPair
candidates.quote: Look for 2 swing lows to form at around the same level ... Look for an earlier swing low which is lower but not too much lower (maybe 1-3 ATR?) that has not yet been taken out. Enter long if a bar has a low below the earliest swing low and a close above it.
candidates.description: The two most recent swing lows sit at about the same level (within an ATR tolerance); the swing low before them is 1-3 ATR lower and has not been traded below since. This bar's low goes below that earlier swing low and the bar closes back above it: long. Short mirrors at swing highs.

complexity.reason: Three pivot occurrences with ATR-scaled relations and an untaken-level test.

library_check.evidence: FailedSwingBreakoutReversal is the same undercut-and-close-back trigger on the MOST RECENT swing low. ON-11 aims it at the THIRD pivot and requires the two newer pivots to form a level 1-3 ATR above it.

notes: Swing strength is not stated (the note says 'identify ATR threshold by eye'); 2 assumed.
'Around the same level' concretized as pairTolAtr; 'lower but not too much lower' as the 1-3 ATR band below the lower of the pair.
'Earlier swing low' concretized as occurrence 3, the pivot immediately before the pair.

candidates.name: LargeShapedBarAtLag
candidates.quote: A large bullish bar (> 2 ATR but less than 7 just to avoid weird case with huge bar ; Open in bottom quarter ; close in top quarter)
candidates.description: The bar `lag` bars ago is a large bull bar of a given shape: range between minRangeAtr and maxRangeAtr x ATR (ATR as of that bar), open in the bottom openFraction of its range, close in the top closeFraction. Short side: a bear bar, open in the top, close in the bottom. Shared by ON-12-b and ON-13, and at other defaults by ON-21 (standard bar) and ON-24 (huge bar).

complexity.reason: Single-bar arithmetic against an ATR read from a series variable.

library_check.evidence: At lag 0 and maxRangeAtr large this is OpenNearBarLow(0.25) AND CloseRangePosition(0.75) AND BarRangeAtrMultiple(2, N) - three existing rules ANDed. The cap, and reading all three at a lag against the ATR as of that bar, are what the pattern rules need and the existing rules lack. ClimaxBar (Brooks) tests a body fraction instead of open/close positions.

notes: ATR length is not given in #12/#13 (the note lists per-timeframe ATR lookbacks for the stops); 20 assumed.
Strict > / < for the size band per the note ('> 2 ATR but less than 7').
CloseRangePosition, one of the three rules this decomposes into at lag 0, is a Davey (EEC) rule: provenance to surface if the authoring pass reuses it.

candidates.name: LargeBarTightPauseNearHigh
candidates.quote: 3-5 subsequent bars are small (< .5 the size of the large bullish bar) and are contained entirely within the range that extends .4*range_of_large_bar above and below the high of the large bar. Enter long
candidates.description: A large bull bar (ON-12-a) N bars ago, and each of the N bars since is smaller than half its range and lies entirely within +/- 0.4 x its range of its high: long on the Nth such bar. Short mirrors around a large bear bar's low.

complexity.reason: Fixed-offset loop over pauseBars bars against one lagged bar.

library_check.evidence: MultiSessionPauseBreakout: a strong leg, a shallow pause inside it, entry on the close beyond the leg extreme. ON-12-b enters on the pause itself (no breakout), from a single large bar, with a size cap on each pause bar and a band centred on the big bar's high (so pause bars may trade above it).

notes: '3-5 subsequent bars' is the pauseBars range; it fires exactly pauseBars bars after the big bar.
Range ideas for the grid: pauseBars 3..5, bandFraction 0.3..0.5.

candidates.name: LargeBarHoldThenCloseThroughMidpoint
candidates.quote: Price holds between the 50% retracement level and 50% extension level for at least 5 bars. Enter short on the first candle to close below the 50% retracement level.
candidates.description: Long side (mirror of the note's short): a large bear bar (ON-12-a, short shape) k bars ago; every close since stayed between its 50% extension below the low and its midpoint, for at least minHoldBars bars; this bar is the first to close above the midpoint: long. The note's trade: a large bull bar holds between midpoint and 50% extension above, short on the first close below the midpoint.

complexity.reason: Bounded backward scan for the anchor bar and a loop over closes since.

library_check.evidence: DeepPullbackRetracementFilter measures how far the close has retraced a window leg; nothing anchors on one large bar's midpoint and requires a hold band of closes for a minimum time before the first close through it.

notes: 'Price holds between' concretized on CLOSES (the trigger is a close); holding on whole-bar highs and lows is the alternative.
The midpoint (50% retracement) is the bar's midpoint for either colour; the 50% extension lies beyond the bar's close-side extreme.
No upper size cap in this note; maxRangeAtr 100 disables it.
maxBars bounds the scan (none in the note).

candidates.name: RsiTightBandExitBarColour
candidates.quote: RSI-14 is in a very tight range (45-55 or 40-60) for at least 5 bars. Next bar (signal) brings RSI out of the range. If signal bar is green, enter long.
candidates.description: RSI was inside a tight band around 50 on each of the previous N bars and this bar's RSI is outside it (either side); a green signal bar means long, a red one short. 20241025.1 (green means short) is the reverse placement.

complexity.reason: RSI series-variable history over a short window.

library_check.evidence: RsiBelowThreshold is a bare threshold. Nothing tests RSI held in a band for N bars and then left it, nor gates on the signal bar's colour.

notes: 45-55 / 40-60 map to bandHalfWidth 5 / 10.
The note does not say which side RSI leaves on; both sides count. A green bar can leave the band downward (close below the prior close after a gap), so this is not the same as 'RSI leaves upward'.
One rule and its reverse: .2 is the plain long, .1 the flip.

candidates.name: LargeBarAtExtremeNextBarExtendsWeakClose
candidates.quote: Large (>1.5 ATR) standard ... bearish bar that closes at or near the 20 bar low. Next bar makes a lower low but closes in the bottom 20% of the large standard bar's range. Enter short.
candidates.description: Long side (mirror of the note): the prior bar is a large standard bull bar (ON-12-a at lag 1: range over 1.5 ATR, open in its bottom third, close in its top third) closing at or near the 20-bar high; this bar makes a higher high and closes in the top 20% of that bar's range (or above it): long.

complexity.reason: Fixed-lag bar arithmetic plus one Highest window.

library_check.evidence: ClimaxBar tests one large trend bar at lag 0 with a body fraction. ON-21 reads the large bar at lag 1, places its close near the window extreme, and needs a follow-through bar that extends AND closes strong. BreakoutBarLargeBodyLargeRange (Brooks) is a lag-0 size and body test only.

notes: The note's 'open and high near opposite extremes' is read as open and CLOSE (a 'standard' trend bar), about 1/3 each.
'At or near the 20 bar low' concretized as within nearAtr ATRs of the 20-bar low (window ending at the large bar, inclusive).
Kept as one pane-1 rule: the near-extreme test and the follow-through bar are both anchored on the lag-1 bar, so they cannot be split into independent placements.

candidates.name: HugeBarOppositeInsideBarThenResume
candidates.quote: Huge bearish bar with open near the high and close near the low that takes out X bar low ... Before the high of that bar gets taken out there is a bullish inside bar with open near low and close near the high. ... Enter short on the close of the first red candle.
candidates.description: Long side (mirror): a huge bull bar b bars ago (ON-12-a shape, range at least K x ATR) whose high took out the prior X-bar high; later a bearish inside bar (open near its high, close near its low); since then nothing has traded below the huge bar's low; this bar is the first green bar after the inside bar: long. The note's trade is the short.
candidates.book_order_type: enter on the first red candle's close; mechanized as next open

complexity.reason: Bounded backward scan with a lagged pattern anchor, an inside-bar search and an invalidation level.

library_check.evidence: InsideBar is the strict single-bar inside test. No rule chains a large breakout bar, a counter-coloured inside bar and a first resumption bar while the large bar's far extreme holds.

notes: 'Huge' has no number: hugeAtr default 2 ATR (the note's other 'large' bars are 1.5-2 ATR).
X (the taken-out window) is 10-50 in the note's two examples; default 20.
'Inside bar' read as inside its immediately preceding bar (strict, the InsideBar convention); inside the huge bar itself is the alternative.
Note: the invalidation is the huge bar's OPEN-side extreme being taken out (the short's 'high of the bearish bar').

candidates.name: BreakoutCandleClassSequence
candidates.quote: A breakout candle can be classified as LOW/HIGH candle or CONSOLIDATION candle. ... Look for the pattern (L-XC-L) or (H-XC-H) where XC means an uninterrupted sequence of CONSOLIDATION candles.
candidates.description: Bars that break the prior N-bar high or low are classed H (close above the prior N-bar high), L (close below the prior N-bar low) or C (broke out but closed back inside). Long: this bar is H, and the breakout candles before it are an uninterrupted run of at least minC C candles preceded by an H. Short mirrors with L-C..C-L.
candidates.book_order_type: next bar after the second H/L candle

complexity.reason: Per-bar classification against a lagged window extreme, scanned back over a variable-length sequence.

library_check.evidence: BothSidedFailedBreakouts / FailedBreakoutReversal / TwiceFailedBreakoutAttempt (Brooks) count failed window breakouts. None classes breakout candles into close-outside vs close-inside and matches a class SEQUENCE.

notes: The note defines HIGH candles as 'a high above the 50-bar high', which would make every upside C candle also H. Read as CLOSE above the prior 50-bar high, symmetric with LOW candles and consistent with the C definition. Flagged for Brian.
The note gives no direction; pane 1's reverse covers both. Written as continuation (H-C..C-H long).
Whether non-breakout bars may sit inside the C run is unresolved (open question); the pseudocode skips them.
maxSpan bounds the backward scan; the per-bar Highest at offset j+1 must be open-coded (function-history read at a variable offset is unregistered).

candidates.name: RedRunThroughStackedSupportFade
candidates.quote: Price is trading in a range (see indicators 20250103.1 and 20250116.2) Contiguous series of red bars break through and close below two support lines. Enter long.
candidates.description: Two stacked support zones (indicator I2: the upper zone entirely above the lower), both valid as of the start of the run. An unbroken run of red bars starts at or above the upper zone, and this bar, still red, is the first in the run to close below the lower zone: long (a fade). Short mirrors with a green run up through two stacked resistance zones. The range condition is pane 2 (I3 / I1).

complexity.reason: Needs the I2 swing-cluster zone detector twice, read as of a past bar, plus a run counter.

library_check.evidence: Depends on the I2 support-zone indicator, which has no library equivalent. LevelTouchCount (Brooks) reads one pivot level, not clustered zones; no rule fades a one-colour run through two levels.

notes: Reading confirmed by Brian 2026-11-05 (TRIAGE #26).
I2 is specced elsewhere (indicators); this candidate assumes it exposes each valid zone's low and high, newest first.
'Starts at or above' read as the run's first open at or above the upper zone's LOW (inside the zone counts as 'at').
Fires on the first close below the lower zone during the run rather than waiting for the run to end, which is the only way to enter on a bar-close signal.
Pane-2 companions: I3 (swing-regression range) or I1 (consolidation bar), not in this file.

candidates.name: NewWindowLowAboveLongerLow
candidates.quote: Signal candle is a large bar (>= 2 ATR14) with a low below the X bar low but above the Y*X (Y ~ 2) low.
candidates.description: This bar's low is below the lowest low of the prior X bars but above the lowest low of the prior Y x X bars: a new short-window low that is not a new long-window low. Long. Short mirrors at highs. 20250208.1b is this rule alone; .1 adds ON-29-b and ON-29-c.
candidates.pseudocode:
longN = (int)(longFactor * lookback);
return low[0] < lowest(low, lookback)[1] && low[0] > lowest(low, longN)[1];

complexity.reason: Two window extremes.

library_check.origin: Davey EEC (HighestHighBreakout, added with the EEC batch 0b6dea8)
library_check.evidence: HighestHighBreakout's short side is low at or below the N-bar lowest low (window including the current bar); placed flipped it is the 'new X-bar low' half. ON-29-a is strict against the window ending one bar ago and adds the outer bound (not a Y x X low), which no rule has. BullReversalBarAtNewLow and FailedBreakoutBeyondExtreme (Brooks) read the same new-low term with other second halves.

notes: X 25-50 (default 25), Y 2-3 (default 2) from the note. Y x X is truncated to an integer bar count.
Split per 'parameterize, don't author twice': .1b = ON-29-a alone, .1 = ON-29-a + ON-29-b + ON-29-c.

candidates.name: LargeBarRange
candidates.quote: Signal candle is a large bar (>= 2 ATR14)
candidates.description: This bar's range is at least K x ATR(14). Direction-agnostic.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] - low[0] >= rangeMultiple * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: One ATR accumulator.

library_check.evidence: BarRangeAtrMultiple(rangeMultiple = 2, atrLookback = 14): el_ge(range, K x WFSafe ATR) on the current bar.

candidates.name: CloseInTopOfBar
candidates.quote: Signal bar's close is in the upper 20% of the bar.
candidates.description: The close sits in the top 20% of the bar's own range (short: bottom 20%).
candidates.pseudocode: (close[0] - low[0]) / (high[0] - low[0] + epsilon) > threshold

complexity.reason: Single-bar arithmetic.

library_check.evidence: CloseRangePosition(threshold = 0.8) is exactly this ratio test, mirrored. Its origin is Kevin Davey's Entry & Exit Confessions: an own idea coinciding with a Davey term.

candidates.name: ConsolidationZone
candidates.quote: Consolidation zone defined over a range of X bars as: (X_bar_high - X_bar_low) < Y*ATRX
candidates.description: The X bars ending `lag` bars ago form a consolidation zone: their highest high minus lowest low is less than Y x ATR(X), the ATR read at the zone's last bar. Exposes zoneHigh and zoneLow. lag 1 is the zone before a breakout bar (ON-30-b, ON-32, ON-33 at their own offsets); lag 0 is the zone the current bar belongs to (ON-34). As a pane-2 condition it is direction-agnostic.
candidates.pseudocode:
zoneHigh = highest(high, X)[lag]; zoneLow = lowest(low, X)[lag];
return zoneHigh - zoneLow < Y * atrVal[lag];   // atrVal = WFSafe_AvgTrueRange(X) series variable

complexity.reason: Two window extremes and an ATR read at a fixed offset.

library_check.evidence: RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple(rangeLookback = X, rangeAtrMultiple = Y, atrLookback = X) is this test at lag 0. Adding a `lag` input (default 0, reading the window and the ATR at that offset) is behaviour-preserving. Residual difference: the library is el_le (at most), the note says strictly less; only an exact tie separates them. TightRangeBlocksEntries is the same arithmetic as a Switch. TRIAGE I5 is the inverse ratio of the same test (one rule).

notes: #30-#33 give no numbers; defaults X 20, Y 3 are placeholders (plausible ranges X 15-40, Y 2-5). #34 uses X 40-60, Y 5-7.
The ATR is read at the zone's last bar so the breakout bar's own true range does not inflate the zone's benchmark; with lag 0 it is the library's current-bar ATR.
ATRX: the ATR length equals the zone length X.

candidates.name: ConsolidationBreakoutBar
candidates.quote: Bullish breakout opens in the consolidation zone and closes at least Z*ATRX above the prior X_bar_high
candidates.description: This bar opens inside the range of the prior X bars and closes at least Z x ATR(X) above their highest high: long. Bearish breakout (opens inside, closes Z ATR below the prior X-bar low): short. Paired in pane 2 with ON-30-a at lag 1. 20250221.2 (#31, the failed-breakout short) is this rule's reverse placement.
candidates.pseudocode:
zh = highest(high, X)[1]; zl = lowest(low, X)[1];
return open[0] >= zl && open[0] <= zh && close[0] >= zh + breakoutAtr * atrVal[1];

complexity.reason: Two window extremes at offset 1 and an ATR read.

library_check.evidence: CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh is close > Highest(High, N)[1]. ON-30-b adds an ATR margin and requires the bar to OPEN inside the prior range (no gap-and-go). BreakoutClearsPriorExtremeByMargin (Brooks) measures the HIGH, in ticks; AtrBandBreakout (original corpus) measures from the Donchian midline.

summary: 27 KEEP rows (#1-#43) specced as candidates: three primitives (the swing-pair box for #1-#3, the shaped large bar for #12/#13/#21/#24, the consolidation zone for #30-#34), pane-1 entries for every row except #31 (which is #30's reverse plus an exit), and pane-2 filters split off where a row ANDs a separable condition (#29, #34, #38/#39, #40, #42). #6, #34 and #42 reduce entirely to existing rules at other parameters; #29 and #42 reuse Davey-catalogued terms (CloseRangePosition, HighestHighBreakout) and #38 uses Davey momentum in pane 2 as allowed.

resolutions.answer: HIGH candle = CLOSE above the 50-bar high (symmetric with LOW). Every bar between the two L's (H's) must be a C candle.
Level = a cluster of wick lows within a tolerance, built like the I2 support zone (not the most recent swing low).

Zone: scanning back N bars, the K+ most recent 1-bar swing lows all within X*ATR of each other, with std dev of those lows <= k*ATR; bottom = lowest of them; a close more than 0.5*ATR below the bottom kills it. #26 needs two distinct stacked zones. No pane-2 'near zone' condition for now.
A bar that is both a swing high and a swing low counts as both, ordered by bar direction: a green bar (close > open) is low-then-high, a red bar high-then-low.
The mirror order (high, low, high, low with the last two inside the first two) also counts.
Breakaway move = a run of consecutive bull bars each with range >= k*ATR; measured from the first run bar's open to the run's highest high.
Cancel the armed setup if a later bar trades back into the band. Add a window input W, counted from the wick bar, constrained W > Z.
'Fractal low length ~3' = swing strength 3 (three bars each side); the pullback must be at least 3 bars.
